problem: VLA navigation policies trained on robot datasets tend to ignore language (posterior collapse) because, for a given observation, the action distribution is nearly unique, so there is little semantic/task diversity per observation. Prior hindsight relabeling (e.g., NaVILA) only labels behaviors that were actually executed.
motivation: Generalist robots should follow fine-grained instructions, but curated data collection for language following is expensive and contradicts training on all available data. If different instructions map to different actions for the same observation, the policy must attend to language; this can be synthesized with VLMs and a simple atomic policy.
key_idea: Use a VLM to generate counterfactual instructions plus atomic commands at decision points of existing trajectories, then use a learned atomic policy to synthesize the corresponding counterfactual actions, yielding many (instruction, action) pairs per observation to train a VLA.
insight: Language following is motivated by conditional mutual information I(a;l|o), lower-bounded by H(l_atomic|o) - H(l_atomic|l,o), so diverse counterfactual instructions with distinct atomic commands raise it. Empirically, adding counterfactuals to the same hindsight labels raises average success by 27% over the standard VLA (which mostly ignores language and only succeeds on well-represented objects). A high-capacity VLM backbone is needed to exploit the diverse labels: ResNet+FiLM with CLIP handles only simple object/atomic commands.
method: Atomic labeling: heuristically discretize trajectories (yaw-change threshold, 10-step window) into {turn left/right, adjust left/right, go forward, stop} segments computed from actions only.
Atomic policy pi_a(a|l_a,o): EfficientNet-b2 image encoder + T5 language embedding + Transformer, with a diffusion action-chunk head, trained on atomic-labeled data; follows simple commands reliably.

Hindsight relabeling: GPT-4o describes subsampled frames, summarizes them into structured instructions (Move to B / away from C / past D), then a second filtering pass with atomic label sequence keeps consistent instructions and adds new ones.

Counterfactual instruction generation: at decision points (atomic segment boundaries), GPT-4o is prompted with images, atomic labels and existing instructions to propose alternative short-horizon behaviors, each with a new instruction and an atomic command.

Counterfactual action synthesis: sample action chunks from pi_a for each counterfactual atomic command at the observation; add (o, l_cf, a_cf) and the original hindsight-labeled tuples to the training set.

CAST-VLA policy: PaliGemma 3B (SigLIP 400M + Gemma 2B, all unfrozen) fine-tuned on the GNM mixture with 128 added action tokens, predicting 16 tokens (8 steps x xy deltas), 100k steps, batch 192, lr 1e-4.

setting.backbone: PaliGemma 3B (SigLIP + Gemma 2B, fine-tuned); labeling by GPT-4o (frozen); atomic policy EfficientNet-b2+T5+diffusion
setting.training_data: GNM navigation data mixture (multi-embodiment indoor/outdoor) augmented with VLM hindsight and counterfactual labels; no additional data collection or human annotation
setting.action_space: predicted xy waypoint deltas (8-step chunk, binned into 128 tokens), converted to velocities by a separate controller

numbers_note: Results are only given in a bar figure (average 53% success, +27% over standard VLA, +19% over prior methods on 27 real-world tasks, 3 environments, 5 trials each) and per-prompt trial counts in an appendix table; no standard benchmark metrics reported.
results: CAST-VLA achieves about 53% average success across 27 real-world instruction-following tasks (office hallway, kitchen, outdoor park), a 27% improvement over the same VLA trained with hindsight labels only. It outperforms CoNVOI (which uses lidar) and pi_a+planning by 19% on aggregate, though CoNVOI is slightly better on object/referential tasks.
limitations: Navigation-specific design (heuristic atomic segmentation from motion, domain-specific prompts); extending to manipulation needs more care.
Still limited by the visual diversity of observations in the dataset.
VLM annotation is slow, imperfect, and quality depends on the model and prompts.
